note: flags from an independent visual reviewer who looked at the compare images

flags.problem: At 1:1 the lattice struts are blurred into soft grey halos with dark smudges at the joints; the crisp 1px original edges are lost. Used on the wall side of the Eiffel tower (wall_side 0.97).
flags.fix: Sharpen the contour edges: use anti-aliased contour fills at 8x instead of PCHIP-blurred shading, and cut the blur radius on the strut edges so joints stay crisp at 1:1.

flags.problem: The original is a flat facade with rectangular recessed panels and pale pilasters. The result is grainy concrete with invented crack arcs and an hourglass shape, plus an obvious mirror-symmetry X seam at the centre. The panel layout and design are not preserved, and the material reads as cracked concrete rather than the plain plaster wall.
flags.fix: Keep the original panel rectangles by taking the low-frequency layout and colour from the original, and inject only fine grain. Drop the mirror-tiled crack source and use offset, non-mirrored tiling so no symmetry axis or invented cracks appear.

flags.problem: The rivet ring is present and positioned correctly at fit view, but the rivet highlights and domes are much dimmer than the original. The plate is nearly flat at 1:1 with almost no visible tooth, so the rivets read as faint specks.
flags.fix: Restore dome contrast (brighter highlight, darker shadow) to match the original rivets, and raise the seeded tooth amplitude so the plate has visible metal grain at 1:1.

flags.problem: The logo design is right at fit view, but at 1:1 the red letter edges and black drop shadow are soft and muddy. The letterforms lose their crisp outline, so this reads as blur rather than flat art.
flags.fix: Rebuild the logo edges from an anti-aliased vector-style contour fill at 4x instead of PCHIP-blurred alpha. Keep the shadow as a hard offset layer and avoid any soft halo around the glyphs.
